package.desc: Primitive proof rules, logical symbols and proof-state control frames.
package.title: Proof toolkit
part.allE.desc: Connect \mark{forall}x. P(x) and choose an object t to obtain P(t).
part.allE.name: Choose an instance
part.allE.settings.t.label: Which thing
part.allI.desc: Name an arbitrary object a on the part. Prove P(a) inside the box and connect it to “Conclusion” to obtain \mark{forall}x. P(x) outside. a must not occur in any open assumption.
part.allI.name: For-any box
part.allI.regions.0.label: Inside
part.allI.settings.x.label: Name
part.andE.desc: Connect A \mark{and} B to get A and B at separate outputs.
part.andE.name: Split
part.andI.desc: Connect A and B to get A \mark{and} B.
part.andI.name: Join
part.append.desc: Connect the results of different proof routes. Continue with the first route that can still proceed, in numbered order.
part.append.name: Join candidates
part.append.settings.ways.label: Routes
part.each.desc: The parts inside run once on each goal, seeing only that goal each time; if any goal fails, the whole part fails.
part.each.name: Each goal in turn
part.each.regions.0.label: Each goal in turn
part.exI.desc: Connect P(t) to obtain \mark{exists}x. P(x), with t as a witness. If exactly one existential statement fits, it is selected automatically; if several fit, choose the conclusion on the part.
part.exI.name: Generalise
part.exI.settings.target.label: Conclusion to derive
part.impI.desc: A box, with A set on the part. Inside, A may be used as an assumption; prove B there and wire it to “Conclusion”, and the part gives A \mark{implies} B.
part.impI.name: Assumption box
part.impI.regions.0.label: Inside
part.impI.settings.A.label: Assume
part.mp.desc: From A \mark{implies} B and A, gives B.
part.mp.name: Apply
part.natInd.desc: Two boxes, proving the \mark{forall}x. P(x) chosen on the part. The first proves P(0); in the second the number is called a (named on the part; it must not occur in any open assumption), P(a) may be used as an assumption, and P(S a) is to be proved. Once both are proved, the part gives \mark{forall}x. P(x).
part.natInd.name: Mathematical induction
part.natInd.regions.0.label: The case 0
part.natInd.regions.1.label: From a to S a
part.natInd.settings.P.label: Prove
part.natInd.settings.x.label: Name
part.orI.desc: Connect A and choose another statement B and its position to get A \mark{or} B or B \mark{or} A. B need not be proved.
part.orI.name: Add alternative
part.orI.settings.other.label: Other side
part.orI.settings.side.label: Other side goes
part.orI.settings.side.options.0.label: Left
part.orI.settings.side.options.1.label: Right
part.refl.desc: Choose a thing t on the part; gives t = t.
part.refl.name: Reflexivity
part.refl.settings.t.label: Which thing
part.repeat.desc: The frame receives the input; its inner output goes to “Result” and back into the frame, round after round, until it stops changing, and the last round’s result is given. If a round fails, it stops at the round before.
part.repeat.name: Repeat frame
part.repeat.regions.0.label: Each round
part.rewrite.desc: Wire in s = t and a sentence containing s; the part marks each s in it, and the ticked ones become t.
part.rewrite.name: Substitute equals
part.rewrite.settings.at.label: Which occurrences to replace
tag.proof.title: Proof rules
